faqs.question: What retirement plan options do business owners have?
faqs.answer: Common options include a SEP IRA, a Solo 401(k) for owners with no employees other than a spouse, a SIMPLE IRA for small businesses with employees, and more complex profit-sharing or defined benefit plans. The right choice depends on staffing, income, how much you want to save, and administrative cost. Contribution limits change every year.

faqs.question: How does self-employment tax work?
faqs.answer: The self-employment tax rate is 15.3%, made up of 12.4% for Social Security and 2.9% for Medicare. It generally applies to 92.35% of net earnings from self-employment, and the Social Security portion is subject to an annual wage limit. It is paid in addition to income tax, typically through quarterly estimated payments.

faqs.question: How much should a business owner set aside for taxes?
faqs.answer: There is no single percentage. The amount depends on your income, deductions, entity type, and state. A CPA can estimate quarterly payments based on your actual numbers, and adjust them during the year.

faqs.question: When should a business owner start succession planning?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most expect, because the options depend on the years available to prepare. A financial plan can model the personal cash-flow and tax effects of a transfer or sale, while an attorney prepares the legal documents.

faqs.question: Why does it help to have a CPA and financial planner work together?
faqs.answer: Entity choice, owner compensation, retirement contributions, and a future sale all affect both the tax return and the long-term plan. When both professionals work from the same information, those effects can be reviewed together before decisions are made.
